title: Real-world Outcomes of Adjuvant Olaparib in gBRCA1/2-Mutated Early Breast Cancer
official: Real-world Outcomes of Adjuvant Olaparib in Patients With Early Breast Cancer and Germline BRCA1 and BRCA2 Pathogenic Variants (REAL-OLA)
summary:
This is a multicenter, observational, study with both retrospective and prospective phase, designed to evaluate the clinicopathologic characteristics and outcomes of patients with HER2-negative early (breast cancer and germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants who receive adjuvant olaparib as part of routine care.

This observatoinal study will address critical evidence gaps and provide comprehensive real-world data, informing clinical practice, improving patient care, and supporting ongoing implementation of genetic-guided personalized oncology in patient with pathigenic variants of BRCA1 or BRCA2.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Age ≥ 18 years (or local age of majority).
2. Histologically confirmed invasive early breast cancer (stage I-III, non-metastatic at diagnosis).
3. Germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 pathogenic or likely pathogenic variant confirmed by accredited genetic testing.
4. HER2-negative tumor (per local pathology; IHC 0-1+ or IHC 2+ with ISH-negative).
5. High-risk features in line with local criteria for adjuvant olaparib use:

   * TNBC: residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, or tumor ≥2 cm or node-positive after adjuvant chemo.
   * HR+/HER2-: ≥4 positive axillary nodes, or 1-3 nodes with additional high-risk features (e.g. high grade, large tumor, CPS+EG score \>3) depending on local reimbursement / guideline rules.
6. Completed (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy with curative intent, including an anthracycline- and/or taxane-based regimen.
7. Started adjuvant olaparib within a predefined interval after completion of (neo)adjuvant therapy (e.g. within 12 weeks after surgery or completion of radiotherapy; record the actual timing).
8. No evidence of distant metastatic disease at the time of starting olaparib.
9. Available baseline clinical, pathologic and treatment data.
10. For the prospective component written informed consent per local regulations.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Metastatic or recurrent breast cancer before starting olaparib.
2. Prior PARP inhibitor exposure for any indication (unless you intentionally allow it and record separately).
3. Other active malignancy (excluding adequately treated non-melanoma skin cancer, in situ carcinoma of cervix, or other cancers in remission \>5 years) if it may confound outcomes, per investigator judgement.
4. For prospective patients: inability or unwillingness to provide informed consent.
